seoTitle: How to Use eBay Local Pickup for Buying & Selling
metaDescription: Learn how eBay Local Pickup works for both buyers and sellers in 2026, from enabling it as a seller to arranging a safe meet-up as a buyer.
intro: Local pickup on eBay is a great option for large or bulky items where shipping isn't practical, letting buyers and sellers arrange an in-person handover instead. This guide covers how it works from both sides of the transaction.

steps.heading: Enable local pickup as a seller
steps.body: When creating your listing, turn on the local pickup option and set your item's general location so nearby buyers can find it.

steps.heading: Communicate with the buyer
steps.body: Once a sale is arranged, message the buyer to agree on a pickup time and location that works for both of you.

steps.heading: Filter for local pickup as a buyer
steps.body: Use eBay's search filters to show only listings offering local pickup within your desired distance.

steps.heading: Arrange a safe meet-up
steps.body: Choose a public, well-lit location for the handover, and consider bringing someone with you for larger transactions.

steps.heading: Mark the item as received
steps.body: As a buyer, confirm receipt on the eBay app or site once you've collected the item to complete the transaction properly.

faq.question: Is local pickup a good option for expensive items on eBay?
faq.answer: Yes, it allows buyers to inspect the item in person before completing the purchase, which can add confidence for higher-value transactions.

faq.question: Does local pickup eliminate shipping fees entirely?
faq.answer: Yes, since there's no shipping involved, sellers avoid shipping costs and delays, and buyers don't pay for delivery.

faq.question: What happens if a buyer doesn't show up for a scheduled pickup?
faq.answer: Sellers should communicate clearly beforehand and may need to contact eBay support if a no-show causes a dispute over the transaction.

faq.question: Is local pickup safe for meeting strangers?
faq.answer: Choosing a public location and bringing someone along are common safety practices, and eBay recommends being cautious just as you would with any in-person transaction.
